subject: science
passage: If most of a spiral galaxy's mass resided where most of its light does, in the bright central bulge, then stars orbiting far from the center ought to move more slowly than those closer in, just as the outer planets of the solar system orbit the Sun more slowly than the inner ones. Measurements made in the 1970s showed otherwise: across many galaxies, orbital speeds remain nearly constant well beyond the visible disk. <u>The most widely accepted interpretation holds that each galaxy is embedded in a vast halo of matter that emits no light.</u> That interpretation, however, rests on the assumption that gravity behaves at galactic scales as it does within the solar system, an assumption that a minority of physicists, proposing modified laws of gravity, have chosen to abandon rather than posit an unseen substance.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It introduces an explanation whose underlying premise the following sentence presents as contestable.
choices.B: It presents the alternative account of the speeds that a minority of physicists have come to favor.
choices.C: It reports the measurements that first revealed the gap between predicted and observed speeds.
choices.D: It resolves the puzzle described earlier by confirming that gravity works the same way at every scale.

explanation.why: The underlined sentence gives the dark-halo explanation for the unexpectedly constant speeds. The next sentence says this explanation "rests on the assumption" that gravity works at galactic scales as it does nearby, an assumption some physicists "abandon." So the sentence introduces an explanation whose foundation is then shown to be disputed.
explanation.A: Correct. The final sentence identifies the assumption beneath the halo explanation and notes that some physicists reject it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The underlined sentence gives the "most widely accepted" view; the minority's modified-gravity account appears in the final sentence.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The measurements are reported in the previous sentence; the underlined sentence interprets them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The halo explanation assumes, rather than confirms, that gravity is the same at all scales, and the next sentence notes that some physicists reject that assumption.
